faq.title: Answers before the first call.
faq.text: The questions teams ask most, answered without the sales detour.

items.a: We build fast, custom websites for B2B companies. The site is code you own, in your repository and on your hosting, instead of a site you rent on a platform.
The code sits in your Git repository. The site runs on your hosting account. The CMS project belongs to you. If we stop working together, the site keeps running.

items.q: Why move off a website platform?
items.a: Platforms cap your CMS items, charge for plugins and seats, lock your hosting, and ship JavaScript you cannot remove. On a phone that means slower pages and lower Core Web Vitals. Code you own removes those limits.

items.q: Which framework do you build in?
items.a: Astro is our default for marketing and content sites. We use Next.js for sites with app logic, auth, or dashboards, and for teams that already work in React. We choose once we know what the site has to do.

items.q: Which CMS will my team use?
items.a: We pick the CMS that fits your team. Sanity suits teams that publish often and want a hosted editor with real-time editing. Payload suits teams that want an open-source CMS inside their Next.js app and repository.

items.q: Will my team still be able to edit content without a developer?
items.a: Yes. Your team edits copy, images, and landing pages in the browser, and the site updates when they publish. You need a developer for new components or structural changes, not for content.

items.q: How does this help with SEO and AI search visibility (AEO)?
items.a: We ship clean HTML that search engines and AI crawlers can read without running JavaScript. Add structured data, semantic markup, and well-organized content, and your pages become easier to index and to cite in AI answers.

items.q: Will I lose my SEO rankings when I move my site?
items.a: Not when the redirect map holds. We keep your URL structure, set up 301 redirects wherever URLs change, and carry over meta tags, schema, and sitemaps. We also watch indexing and rankings after launch to catch problems early.

items.q: How long does a project take?
items.a: A typical marketing site takes 3 to 4 weeks, depending on the number of pages, custom components, and CMS complexity. A focused landing page or microsite can go live in 1 to 2 weeks. You get a timeline up front, with milestones you can review along the way.

items.q: Can you integrate with our existing marketing stack?
items.a: Yes. Google Analytics, GTM, HubSpot, Segment, Meta Pixel, Hotjar, and most A/B testing tools work with both Astro and Next.js. We set up tracking and event measurement during the build, so you can measure your campaigns from day one.

items.q: Do I pay platform fees after launch?
items.a: No platform plan and no plugin licenses. You pay your hosting and CMS providers directly, on your own accounts. Most marketing sites fit a free or entry hosting tier, Sanity has a free plan, and Payload is open source.
We offer maintenance and ongoing optimization, from weekly Core Web Vitals reports to new landing pages and A/B test support. Your next developer can also pick up the repo without us.

faq.q: Which platforms can you migrate from?

faq.q: Will the site look different?
faq.a: No, unless you want it to. The default is a faithful rebuild: same design, same content, same URLs, new foundation underneath.

faq.q: What do you rebuild it in?
faq.a: Astro for most marketing and content sites, because it serves finished HTML with almost no JavaScript. Next.js if the site has app logic, auth, or dashboards, or your team already works in React. Any engineer you hire later can pick up either one.

faq.q: Can marketing still publish without a developer?
faq.a: Yes, and we treat that as a requirement. Your content lives in a headless CMS your team edits in the browser, and we set it up before we write the first component.

faq.q: Which CMS will my team use?
faq.a: We pick the CMS that fits your team. Sanity gives you a hosted editor with real-time editing. Payload gives you an open-source CMS inside a Next.js app. Both structure content around your pages instead of one big rich-text field.

faq.q: Will I lose my SEO rankings when I move?
faq.a: Not when the redirect map holds. We keep your URL structure, set up 301 redirects wherever URLs change, and carry over meta tags, schema, and sitemaps. We also watch indexing and rankings after launch to catch problems early.

faq.q: What happens to my CMS content and blog posts?
faq.a: We export your CMS content and move it into the new CMS. Your posts, images, and metadata come over intact, and your team edits them in an editor structured around your content.

faq.q: Will there be any downtime during the migration?
faq.a: No. We build and test on a staging environment, then switch over at the DNS level once you have signed off. That keeps downtime close to zero.

faq.q: What about my forms, integrations, and third-party tools?
faq.a: We rebuild and reconnect your forms, analytics, CRM, email tools, and other integrations, then test each one before launch so you lose no leads or data.

servicePages.metaDescription: We profile your site on a real phone, cut what slows the first paint, and ship Core Web Vitals in the green, with the before and after reports to prove it.
servicePages.subtitle: We profile your site on a real phone, find what slows the first paint, and ship the fixes. You get Core Web Vitals in the green and the raw reports that prove it.
servicePages.painTitle: What a slow site costs you.

pain.title: You pay twice for every visitor.
pain.text: Ads and content bring someone to the page, then a four-second paint sends them back to the search results. You paid for that click and got nothing for it.

pain.title: Google ranks the wait.
pain.text: Core Web Vitals are a ranking signal. A failing largest contentful paint holds a page down, however good the copy on it is.

pain.title: The desktop score is not the problem.
pain.text: A green number on a desktop test means little when your buyer is on a mid-range Android over 4G. We test on that device.

works.title: The critical path
works.text: Render-blocking scripts and stylesheets come out of the head, we preload and metric-match the fonts, and the browser paints text on the first pass instead of the third.

works.title: The JavaScript you ship and never run
works.text: Most sites download a whole framework to animate three sections. We cut what is dead, defer what can wait, and load the rest only where it earns its bytes.

works.title: Media that holds the paint hostage
works.text: We size and convert hero images and serve them at the width the layout asks for. Video that autoplays above the fold stops blocking the first frame.

works.title: Layout shift
works.text: We reserve space for whatever arrives late: images, embeds, and the font swap that drops your headline one line down the page.

servicePages.proofText: The same tests, run before and after, with the raw reports attached. You see what moved, and by how much, on the pages you care about.

faq.q: How fast can you make my site?
faq.a: We profile the site first, tell you what each fix is worth, and you decide how far down the list to go. On a tuning pass we promise the measurement. On a new build or a migration, we guarantee 90+ on mobile on the pages we agree on.

faq.q: Will you break my design?
faq.a: No. Speed work is plumbing: the page looks the same and arrives sooner. Anything that would change a layout goes on a staging URL for you to review before it ships.

faq.q: What if my platform is the bottleneck?
faq.a: Then we tell you. Every builder has a ceiling, and we know where it sits: what to cut, what to move out of the head, and the point where the honest answer is a rebuild in code you own.

faq.q: How long does it take?
faq.a: A typical pass runs one to two weeks from audit to shipped, depending on how much of the site is custom and how soon your review comes back.

servicePages.ctaText: We run the audit and reply within a day with what we would fix first and what it is worth.

servicePages.metaDescription: We structure your pages so ChatGPT, Claude, Perplexity and Google AI Overviews quote you by name instead of a competitor, and we measure it on the same prompts.

servicePages.painTitle: Why the answer names someone else.

pain.title: The click is disappearing.
pain.text: Your buyer asks a model instead of typing a query, reads the answer it gives, and never sees the ten blue links you optimized for.

pain.title: Models quote what they can parse.
pain.text: A page built out of nested divs and text baked into images gives a model nothing to lift. Structure, a clear question, and a direct answer give it a paragraph to quote.

pain.title: You cannot win a question you never answer.
pain.text: Most sites describe a product. An answer engine looks for the sentence that answers your buyer’s question, in the words they asked it.

servicePages.painCta: Send us what the model said

works.title: Structured data that matches the page
works.text: Organization, Person, Service, FAQPage and breadcrumbs, wired into one entity graph so a crawler knows what the company is and who stands behind it, instead of nine disconnected blobs.

works.title: Answers written to be lifted
works.text: The question goes in a heading and the answer goes in the first two sentences under it. A model reaches the part worth quoting without wading through a preamble.

works.title: Crawlable to the machines that matter
works.text: A robots.txt that lets GPTBot, ClaudeBot and PerplexityBot in, a sitemap that stays current on its own, and content that renders in HTML rather than after a JavaScript bundle.

works.title: Entity signals off the page
works.text: The profiles, mentions and links that tell a search engine which company owns your name. Most AEO work skips this part, and it decides whether you show up at all.

servicePages.proofTitle: How you tell whether it worked.
servicePages.proofText: We record the answers first: the same prompts, in the same models, before anything changes. After the work we run them again and you see where your name now appears and where it still does not. No agency dashboard, just the transcripts.
servicePages.proofCta: Run the prompts on your site

faq.q: What is AEO and how is it different from SEO?
faq.a: SEO earns a link in a list. AEO earns a sentence inside the answer. The work overlaps, since both want a fast, crawlable, well-structured page, but AEO aims at being quoted rather than clicked.

faq.q: Can you guarantee ChatGPT will mention me?
faq.a: No, and anyone who guarantees it is selling you something. Models change and none of them publishes a ranking. We remove the reasons a model has to skip you, then measure the difference on the same prompts.

faq.q: Does AEO work hurt my Google rankings?
faq.a: The opposite. Structured data, fast pages and clear answers are what classic SEO has asked for all along. AEO is that same work, aimed at a reader that happens to be a model.

faq.q: How long does it take to see results?
faq.a: Crawlers can pick up technical fixes and structured data within weeks. Lasting authority and citations usually take a few months. Timelines vary with competition and how much content needs work, and we give you a realistic outlook after the audit.

faq.q: Do site speed and performance affect AEO?
faq.a: Yes. Crawlers access and process fast, well-structured pages more easily, and your visitors get a better experience too. That is why we combine AEO with web performance work instead of treating them separately.

faq.q: Will AEO work for a B2B company?
faq.a: Yes. B2B buyers research heavily and often ask AI tools to explain products, compare options, and assess credibility. Clear, accurate content helps you show up in those conversations.

faq.q: How do I get started?
faq.a: Book a call. We review your current site, see how AI tools talk about your brand today, and outline a plan with priorities and next steps.

migrationPages.metaDescription: We move your Webflow site to Astro: same design, every URL kept, CMS collections exported, interactions rebuilt, and a repo your team owns.
migrationPages.titleStart: Move from Webflow to Astro and keep
migrationPages.subtitle: We rebuild your Webflow site in Astro to match the one you have, move your CMS collections to the CMS that fits your team, rebuild the interactions that matter, and hand you a repository you own. Your traffic stays where it is.

pain.title: Every page loads jQuery and the interaction engine.
pain.text: Webflow ships jQuery and its own webflow.js on every page, whether that page animates or not. On a phone, that weight is the gap between green and red Core Web Vitals.

pain.title: Only one person dares touch the styles.
pain.text: A few years of combo classes and one-off overrides later, changing a button means checking forty pages. The designer who built it becomes the only safe pair of hands.

pain.title: The CMS plan sets your content strategy.
pain.text: Collection and item caps tied to your plan mean a growing blog, a docs section, or a set of comparison pages hits a plan limit before it runs out of ideas.

works.title: Export, then inventory
works.text: Webflow’s code export leaves the CMS behind, so we pull every collection out through the API, then crawl the live site to catch anything that only exists in production.

works.title: Combo classes, untangled
works.text: Your classes, combo classes, and swatches become a small set of design tokens and components. Same pixels, but a button now changes in one place.

works.title: Interactions rebuilt, not embedded
works.text: Webflow Interactions become CSS and small scripts that load only on the pages that use them, instead of one engine on every page.

works.title: URL parity, checked line by line
works.text: Collection URLs keep their paths, the 301s you already set in Webflow move to the new host, and we diff the two sitemaps before the DNS switch.

migrationPages.proofText: A Git repository with the full history, a build that runs on your own hosting, your content in a CMS your team edits, the redirect map, and the speed reports before and after. No Webflow plan to renew, and no part of the site needs us around to keep it running.

faq.q: How long does a Webflow to Astro migration take?
faq.a: Most marketing sites take 3 to 4 weeks. Sites with several CMS collections and a team that publishes every week take 5 to 6. You get the timeline before anything starts.

faq.q: Can’t I just use Webflow’s code export?
faq.a: You can, but you get a snapshot, not a site. The export leaves your CMS content out, keeps jQuery and webflow.js on every page, and hands you generated files nobody wants to maintain. We rebuild instead, so your team gets code it can work in.

faq.q: What if my Webflow site is turning into an app?
faq.a: Then we build it in Next.js instead. Astro is the default for marketing sites. Logins, dashboards, or a team that already works in React point to Next.js, and the rest of the move stays the same.

faq.q: What happens to my Webflow CMS collections?
faq.a: We export every collection, including rich text, images, references, and SEO fields, and move it into the CMS that fits your team, Sanity or Payload. Every item keeps its slug, so its URL does not change.

faq.q: Can you rebuild Webflow interactions and animations?
faq.a: Yes. Most Webflow interactions become plain CSS transitions or a few lines of script. Heavier scroll timelines get GSAP, loaded only on the pages that use it.

faq.q: Will I lose my Google rankings when I leave Webflow?
faq.a: Not when the redirect map holds. Every URL that earns traffic keeps its path, the 301s you set in Webflow move across, meta tags and schema come with the content, and we watch Search Console through the first month.

faq.q: What happens to my Webflow forms?
faq.a: Webflow forms only work on Webflow hosting, so we reconnect each one to your CRM, email tool, or a form service, and test every submission before launch.

faq.q: Will my team miss the Webflow Editor?
faq.a: Not for long. The new CMS is built around your content: fields for what each page needs, a live preview, and no way to nudge a layout out of place by accident.

faq.q: What does the site cost to run after I cancel Webflow?
faq.a: For most marketing sites, close to nothing. A static Astro site runs on the free or entry tiers of Vercel, Netlify, or Cloudflare. Sanity has a free plan that covers many marketing teams, and Payload is open source. If you need a paid plan, we tell you before work starts. Keep your Webflow plan until the new site is live, then cancel it.

migrationPages.ctaText: We reply within a day with what the move involves and where Webflow is costing you.

migrationPages.metaDescription: Framer site slow on phones, or locked to one plan? We rebuild it in Astro from your Framer project: animations kept, CMS moved, and code you own and can host anywhere.
migrationPages.titleStart: Framer to Astro: keep the design, lose the
migrationPages.subtitle: Framer is a great place to design a site and a heavy way to serve one. We rebuild yours in Astro from the Framer project itself, keep the animations worth keeping, move your CMS to one that fits your team, and hand you code you can host anywhere.

pain.title: Fast on your laptop, slow on their phone.
pain.text: Framer serves every page as a React app. A phone has to download and run that code before the page settles, so the site that feels instant in the editor scores red on a mid-range Android.

pain.title: The layer you hid on mobile still ships.
pain.text: Breakpoints in Framer share one layer tree. The desktop hero you hid on phones and the phone version you hid on desktop both go down the wire to every visitor.

pain.title: There is no code to take with you.
pain.text: Framer has no export. The design, the CMS, and every URL live on its plan, and the plan decides your page, CMS, and bandwidth limits.

works.title: Rebuilt from the project, not a screenshot
works.text: We work inside your Framer project and take spacing, type, and colors straight from it. Desktop, tablet, and phone breakpoints become one responsive layout instead of three stacked copies.

works.title: Animations kept, runtime dropped
works.text: Appear effects, hover states, and scroll transforms become CSS and a few lines of script. Your headline is on screen in the first paint instead of waiting for a script to fade it in.

works.title: Code components carried over
works.text: Your code components are React, and Astro runs React. They come across as islands that load only on the pages that use them, and we rewrite overrides as plain scripts.

works.title: CMS out, slugs intact
works.text: Every Framer CMS collection moves into the CMS that fits your team, with its fields, images, and slugs. The redirects in your Framer site settings move to the new host, so your URLs stay put.

migrationPages.proofText: The site as code in a Git repository, a build you can host anywhere, your content in a CMS your team edits, the redirect map, and phone speed reports before and after. Your designer can keep Framer as a design tool. The live site just stops depending on it.

faq.q: How long does a Framer to Astro migration take?
faq.a: Most Framer sites take 3 to 4 weeks. They tend to have fewer templates and more animation, so the time goes into motion rather than layouts. Sites with several CMS collections and custom code components take 5 to 6.

faq.q: Can’t I just export the code from Framer?
faq.a: No. Framer has no official export, and third-party tools that scrape a Framer site give you the same React runtime in a folder. A rebuild gets you code that is fast on a phone and yours to change.

faq.q: What if my Framer site is turning into an app?
faq.a: Then we build it in Next.js instead. Astro is the default for marketing sites. Logins, dashboards, or a team that already works in React point to Next.js, and the rest of the move stays the same.

faq.q: Will my Framer animations survive the move?
faq.a: Yes. Appear effects, hovers, and scroll transforms come across, rebuilt in CSS and small scripts. Heavier sequences get GSAP, loaded only on the pages that use it. If motion only exists to look busy, we flag it and ask before we cut it.

faq.q: What happens to my Framer CMS collections?
faq.a: We move every collection into Sanity or Payload, whichever fits your team, item by item, with its fields, images, and slug. A post at /blog/your-post stays at /blog/your-post.

faq.q: What about my code components and overrides?
faq.a: Code components move across as React islands, so they keep working and load only where they appear. Overrides become plain scripts, which usually end up shorter than the originals.

faq.q: Can my designer keep designing in Framer?
faq.a: Yes. Framer stays a great design tool. Your designer draws new sections there, we build them into components in the repo, and marketing publishes content in the CMS without touching layout.

faq.q: Will I lose my Google rankings when I leave Framer?
faq.a: Not when the redirect map holds. Every URL keeps its path, the redirects from your Framer site settings move across, page titles and descriptions come with the content, and we watch Search Console through the first month.

faq.q: What happens to my Framer forms?
faq.a: Framer forms send submissions through Framer, so they stop when the site leaves. We reconnect each one to your CRM, email tool, or a form service, and test every submission before launch.

migrationPages.ctaText: We run it on a real phone and reply within a day with what the move involves and what Framer’s runtime costs you on mobile.
